sentence: This project builds a system that collects and analyzes data about aircraft location and motion to study safe management of complex airspace.
This project uses machine learning to study how a computer can find musical motifs and how the brain encodes musical features.
This project builds a mathematical framework to study how networks of simple building blocks can generate complex patterns of activity in the brain.
This project builds imaging agents made with iron and cobalt that can sense redox changes in biological systems using magnetic resonance imaging.
This project develops a way to train deep learning models so that their accuracy stays under control when solving equations based on physics.
This project develops a method that uses equations to study the genetic history of human populations formed by interbreeding.
This project builds a computer model to study how the land and mantle of Antarctica move and change shape as ice melts.
This project supports a conference where researchers share work that links computation, biology and nanotechnology through molecular programming.
This project looks at how a supercomputer that blends virtual and physical settings could be used for real-time problem solving and learning.
This project builds fairness into computer programs that find unusual items in data, so they do not discriminate against some groups.
This project studies chemistry questions such as how proteins and antibodies interact and how catalyst structure affects making renewable fuels.
This project studies how string theory connects to what is observed in the universe, using machine learning and quantum information methods.
This project uses artificial intelligence and atomistic simulations to study how hydrogen moves through grain boundaries in metals.
This project builds deep learning tools that predict what proteins do, and explains how those tools reach their answers.
This project builds an open-source system that makes lists of software components harder to tamper with and easier to check.
This project studies the mathematics of materials that conduct electricity on the surface but not inside, especially when they are disordered.
This project builds ways to shrink large simulation data while keeping the topological features that scientists need for analysis.
This project builds modeling tools that predict how materials made of stiff panels and flexible hinges change shape under loads.
